purpose: Measure the exact registered wide VCP defaults independently of portfolio slots and leader-only gates
hypothesis: The wide multiscale VCP candidate stream may capture market-relative expansion outside the leader representation; measure fixed-horizon selection quality separately from default exits.
research_role: Descriptive training baseline; no automatic temporal-test promotion or parameter selection
required_outputs: Signal counts, executable fills and rejection reasons under original defaults; full mode removes portfolio competition, not execution constraints.
40-session market-relative return and actual-exit return reported separately, with yearly sample sizes and Alpha.
MFE 20/50/100 percent counts and rates, signal-date concentration and repeated-symbol concentration.

Any later cup/flag overlap comparison uses the common training interval and identifies signal-date overlap separately from repeated-stock overlap. Winner counts alone are not recall without a common opportunity denominator.

decision_rules.selection_supported: At least 100 complete paths, positive mean 40-session market-relative return and positive means in at least four training years; otherwise descriptive evidence only.
decision_rules.exit_research: If selection is supported but default realized Alpha is nonpositive, identify the responsible exit paths before proposing one structural change.
decision_rules.failure: Retain all evidence; do not remove RS, trend, scale or exit thresholds by searching this result.
decision_rules.temporal_test: Not authorized by this descriptive protocol. Prior 2023-2026 exposure remains recorded; a clean holdout cannot be reconstructed by renaming dates.

evidence_gap.legacy_candidate_script: scripts/analyze_vcp_breakout_candidates.py sets RS85, distance-high and entry overrides; its full mode is not the original default stream.
evidence_gap.gate_funnel_script: scripts/analyze_vcp_gate_funnel.py uses vcp_leader_breakout, not the wide defaults.

execution: Queue after either active cup or flag v2 run finishes; at most two concurrent research runs. No new data acquisition.
